title: Event Gatekeeper: real-time fanout + policy layer for console usage streams
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce an Event Gatekeeper microservice that sits at the ingress of console usage telemetry. The Gatekeeper validates, enriches, applies tenant-level policies, performs lightweight deduplication and sampling, and deterministically fans events to downstream processors (real-time aggregators, long-term analytics, alerts). It should be low-latency (~5–15ms p99 added), horizontally scalable, and provide backpressure signals to upstream queues when downstream capacity is constrained.
background: Current pipeline pushes raw console events directly into a shared stream and relies on downstream consumers to do validation and routing. This results in duplicated effort, inconsistent sampling and throttling per-tenant, and makes it hard to implement global policy changes (e.g., privacy redaction, per-tenant retention). Several recent incidents (see ENG-54123 and ENG-41209) highlighted variable latencies and cascading consumer failures during traffic spikes.
technical_design:
Gatekeeper will be implemented as a stateless front-end service with an optional small Redis-backed local cache for idempotency checks and tenant configuration. It will accept events via an internal gRPC entrypoint and a fallback HTTP endpoint. Design properties:
- Schema validation using a compiled AVRO/Protobuf registry. Invalid events are rejected with metrics and routed to a dead-letter queue.
- Enrichment hooks: lightweight lookups (tenant metadata, region) using a strongly-consistent config store (DynamoDB/KV store) with cached TTL.
- Deterministic fanout: compute a fanout key (tenant_id + event_type) and map to downstream topics using a routing table service. Fanout can produce 1..N copies depending on feature flags (e.g., to replicate to anomaly-detector and billing-aggregator).
- Backpressure: Gatekeeper tracks downstream publish ACK latency and queue lengths; when thresholds exceeded, Gatekeeper will: 1) signal upstream producer (if supported), 2) apply adaptive sampling per-tenant, and 3) route to durable S3-backed write-ahead log for deferred processing.
- Exactly-once-ish semantics: Use per-event dedupe window (configurable TTL per-tenant) with Redis unique key. For higher guarantees, Gatekeeper can attach idempotency tokens that downstream consumers can use.
api_contract:
gRPC: Ingest(Event) -> Ack{status, deferred:bool, error_code}
HTTP: POST /v1/events -> 202/429/400
Config API (internal): GET /v1/routing/{tenant} -> list of destinations and sampling policies
All endpoints must include tenant_id header; auth via mTLS and service token.
data_flow:
1) Producers -> Gatekeeper gRPC/HTTP
2) Gatekeeper validates/enriches -> publishes to Kafka topics per-destination (or durable WAL if overloaded)
3) Downstream processors (real-time aggregator, anomaly, billing) subscribe to their topic partitions
4) Gatekeeper emits routing telemetry to console-metrics (latency, fanout-count, sample-rate) and to trace spans for request flow
performance_targets:
- 99th percentile added latency at Gatekeeper: <= 15ms for events < 1KB
- Throughput: single instance baseline 5k evt/s; cluster scalable to 200k evt/s with autoscaling
- Error budget: < 0.01% rejected-valid events per day
- Fanout jitter: downstream publish within 50ms p95 of ingress
deployment_plan:
Phased rollout:
1) Nightly deploy to staging with full traffic replay and load tests (2 weeks).
2) Canary region: route 5% of low-risk tenants (no sensitive PII) via feature flag for 48h; monitor error rates and latency.
3) Gradual ramp: 5->25->50->100% over a week with per-tenant opt-out.
4) Switch critical tenants when metrics stable.
Use release: console-2026.04-gatekeeper
rollback_plan:
- Feature flags to disable Gatekeeper per-tenant and redirect producers back to original topic.
- If persistent errors or latency regressions, rollback to previous service revision and enable WAL-to-batch processor to drain queued events.
- Postmortem and follow-up fixes must be submitted before re-rollout.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Key metrics: ingest_rate, reject_rate, enrichment_errors, fanout_count, downstream_publish_latency (p50/p95/p99), wal_write_rate, sampling_applied_count.
Alerts: Reject rate > 0.1% sustained for 5m (P0), downstream_publish_latency p99 > 300ms (P1), WAL growth > 1GB/min (P1).
Tracing: OpenTelemetry spans tagged with tenant_id, event_type, routing_key. Dashboards: Gatekeeper Overview + per-tenant routing heatmap.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for schema validation and routing logic.
- Integration tests: gatekeeper <-> local Kafka & Redis, simulate downstream lag and verify WAL fallback.
- Chaos tests: inject failures in routing service, config store, and downstream brokers.
- Performance tests: synthetic load generator to validate scaling and latency targets.
- Canary verification: synthetic golden events per tenant to ensure fidelity of enrichment and dedupe.
risks:
- Redis cache hot keys for large tenants could create contention. Mitigation: shard dedupe keys by hash and use local caches.
- Increased operational complexity with another critical service in the ingest path. Mitigation: keep Gatekeeper lean, push heavy enrichment to asynchronous processors.
- Potential to lose events if WAL handling is buggy. Mitigation: end-to-end integrity checks and periodic WAL replays into test consumer.
